turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c012, c047, c003, c031,
c088".
turns.answer_text:
I treated this as a small composition-property regression problem and compared the pool compositions against the high-zT regions in the training set. The strongest candidate motifs in the training data were:

- Te–Pb near 0.5/0.45, with a very high nearby training value around zT ≈ 0.78.
- Nearly pure Sn fraction around 0.55, with a training value around zT ≈ 0.71.
- Mg–Sn–Si compositions, several in the 0.5–0.65 range.
- Sb–Co with small In/Fe-type perturbations, including one nearby high value around zT ≈ 0.70.
- Sb–Mg–Bi/Te variants are also promising, but the closest no-Co training analogs were somewhat lower.

Based on nearest high-performing analogs and local consistency, my top selections are:

1. c037 — very close to the high-performing Te/Pb composition.
2. c010 — very close to the high-performing Sn-rich composition.
3. c049 — close to high Mg–Sn–Si training compositions.
4. c096 — close to a strong Sb–Co–In region.
5. c046 — Mg–Sn–Si/Sn-rich composition near other high Mg–Sn–Si examples.

Final: c037, c010, c049, c096, c046
